meta.summary: A dark, cinematic marketing system where motion behaves like instrumentation: rules draw across the grid, content slides in a short distance from the reading-start edge, and small labels decode through random characters as if resolving live data. Durations are long and eased with a steep exponential out-curve, so things arrive fast and then settle for a long time, which reads as confident and heavy rather than playful. Interaction is quiet and typographic (sibling dimming, underline sweeps, quarter-turn icons) while a smooth-scrolled, WebGL-backed page and a scale-crossfade route transition make the whole site feel like one continuous application. Navigation gets out of the way in proportion to scroll and comes back instantly on upward intent.

principles.description: Almost every entrance uses an exponential ease-out at 1000 to 1500ms. Most of the distance is covered in the first 20% of the time, then the element drifts into place.
principles.how_to_apply: Use ease-out-expo with slow or cinematic durations for entrances. Never use springs or overshoot. Keep hover and state feedback at 300ms with a gentle ease-out.

principles.principle: Draw the structure, then fill it
principles.description: Hairline rules draw left to right before or alongside the content that sits on them.
principles.how_to_apply: Pair every row or card entrance with a rule-draw on its divider, starting at the same moment, with content offset by a 200ms base delay and 100ms per child.

principles.description: Things enter from the left, exit to the right, underlines draw from the left and wipe out to the right.
principles.how_to_apply: Use x -10% for entrances and +10% for exits. Flip transform-origin to the trailing edge for retractions. Mirror all of this for right-to-left locales.

principles.principle: Text resolves, it does not bounce
principles.description: Short labels and descriptions decode through random characters; headings reveal line by line behind a mask. Body copy is never split.
principles.how_to_apply: Reserve text-scramble-decode for labels, eyebrows, menu titles and one-line descriptions; reserve hero-line-mask-reveal for the single primary heading per page.

principles.description: Hover states change opacity, underline, fill or a quarter-turn of an icon. Elements do not lift, glow or bounce.
principles.how_to_apply: Prefer opacity, background wipes and transform-origin sweeps. Scale only media inside a clipped frame, never the card.

principles.principle: Chrome yields to content in proportion to intent
principles.description: The header hides at a rate tied to scroll distance (half rate going down, full rate coming back up) and frosts only once the page has moved.
principles.how_to_apply: Drive header offset from accumulated scroll delta, clamp to its height, and never animate it on a timer.

principles.description: Smooth scrolling, a scale-crossfade route transition and a WebGL layer synced to DOM sections remove the feeling of page loads.
principles.how_to_apply: Freeze the outgoing page in place, reset scroll invisibly, and run page-transition-scale-crossfade then page-transition-settle-in (two 350ms phases). Start hero entrances only after the transition ends.

principles.principle: Disclose on intent, not by default
principles.description: Menus, card descriptions and accordion content stay hidden until hover, focus or tap, and touch devices get an automatic reveal instead of a hover.
principles.how_to_apply: Gate hover reveals behind (hover: hover); on touch, trigger the same reveal once on in-view.

libraries.name: Hydra framework (proprietary creative-studio framework with its own TweenManager, SplitText, Scroll, Slider, Interaction and WebGL renderer)
libraries.evidence: Global flag CREATED_WITH_HYDRAX, class registry in app bundle (TweenManager, SplitText, Slider, Interaction, RenderManager, FXScene, UIL)

libraries.name: Lenis
libraries.evidence: Separate lenis bundle with embedded version string; global instance with duration 0.8, lerp false, Quart.Out easing, syncTouch false

libraries.name: Custom WebGL renderer (three.js-style scene graph inside the framework)
libraries.evidence: Compiled shader bundle preloaded, single fixed full-viewport canvas, per-slice meshes with scroll uniforms, GPU tier detection scripts

libraries.name: Headless CMS with live visual editing
libraries.evidence: Stega-encoded strings cleaned before text animations; page content delivered as JSON slices

settings.nested_instances: mobile menu, dropdowns, search results, location modal
settings.scroll_lock: reference-counted pauser: lenis.stop() when the first overlay opens, start() when the last closes

motion_system.personality: cinematic and restrained: long exponential settles, technical decode text, typographic hovers

easings.usage: Dominant entrance curve: slide-in-from-start, rule-draw, hero reveals, counters, chart draws, exits of reveals.
Menus, panel heights, header frost, card disclosure, carousel snap, sibling dimming.
Programmatic header hide and show, symmetric fades of section content, vertical slide swaps.
Accordions, row fill wipes, modal blur and scrim, page transition phase 1.
Page transition phase 2 (incoming page settle and overlay out).
CSS hover and state transitions (300ms): colour, opacity, icon rotation, media zoom, mobile menu screens.
CSS opacity and translate toggles for floating buttons and banners.
Infinite loops (marquee, spinners), frame-synced WebGL uniforms.

distances.reveal_offset: translateX(-10%) of the element's own width for content; translateY(100%) of line height for masked heading lines
distances.hover_lift: none (no card lift anywhere); media inside cards scales 1.05 to 1.1
distances.parallax_range: none in DOM; WebGL layers track DOM positions 1:1
distances.slide_distance: 100% of panel width for drawers, mobile menu and side panels

tokens.entrance_exit_ratio: Reveal exits run at about 0.5x the entrance (700ms out vs 1500ms in for rows; scrim 300ms out vs 600ms in). Overlays that hold spatial context are symmetric (modal 1000/1000, side panel 250/250, page transition 350/350). Dimming is asymmetric the other way: highlight in 150ms, restore 500ms.

patterns.name: page-load-progress-bar
patterns.exit_behaviour: On completion snaps to 100% over 200ms, waits 200ms, fades to opacity 0 over 200ms, then is removed from the DOM.
patterns.interruptible: Fake progress: increments shrink as progress rises (+10% below 20%, +4% to 50%, +2% to 80%, +0.5% to 99%) every 1000ms and cap at 99.4% until the real done() fires. Re-used as a route-change ticker with an expected duration of 2000ms and linear bar transitions.
patterns.applies_to: Global: first load and every client-side route change.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Keep; it is a thin, non-intrusive indicator. No change needed.
patterns.ux_purpose: Reduces perceived wait while a heavy WebGL/CMS payload boots, without a blocking splash screen; the page underneath stays a calm solid field.

patterns.name: hero-line-mask-reveal
patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit. Leaves with the page transition.
patterns.interruptible: Split is reverted and re-run on resize or content change; a queued flag prevents overlapping splits.
patterns.applies_to: Primary hero headings on landing and section heroes.
patterns.responsive_differences: Same motion; line breaks re-computed per viewport. Heading min-width changes (full width under 769px).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: None in the source for this pattern (it plays regardless of prefers-reduced-motion). Recommended for replicas: skip the tween and set the end state instantly.
patterns.ux_purpose: Gives the first heading a deliberate, one-line-at-a-time cadence that reads as a statement, and holds attention on the headline before media and secondary text settle.

patterns.name: hero-media-fade
patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit.
patterns.interruptible: Media element is swapped (destroyed and rebuilt) when the viewport aspect ratio crosses to a closer-matching source; the swap is not animated.
patterns.applies_to: Hero background video or image; hero short labels fade to a reduced opacity target (about 0.6) instead of 1.
patterns.responsive_differences: Hero media height is a viewport-relative value (about 96svh with no title, about 76svh with a title). A portrait or landscape source is chosen by nearest aspect angle.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: None in the source for this pattern (it plays regardless of prefers-reduced-motion). Recommended for replicas: skip the tween and set the end state instantly.
patterns.ux_purpose: Media arrives softly behind the headline so the headline wins the first beat, then the atmosphere fills in.
patterns.snippet:
import { gsap } from 'gsap';
export const heroMediaFade = (el) => gsap.fromTo(el, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 1, ease: 'expo.out' });

patterns.name: text-scramble-decode

trigger.start: element 5% visible (or on panel open / hover)

patterns.exit_behaviour: Can run in reverse (progress 1 to 0) to scramble text away; normally no exit.
patterns.interruptible: Each call increments an id; stale runs stop themselves. The loop stops early if progress has not changed for 3 frames, and always restores the clean text on complete or interrupt.
patterns.applies_to: Small uppercase labels, eyebrow text, card descriptions revealed on hover, menu section titles, hero sub-labels and hero descriptions.
patterns.responsive_differences: Card descriptions scramble on hover on pointer devices and on in-view on touch.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: skip the scramble and show clean text immediately.
patterns.ux_purpose: A terminal-style decode that signals live, technical, machine-generated information. It makes short copy feel like it is being resolved rather than faded in, and gives static labels a moment of attention without moving layout.

patterns.name: rule-draw

trigger.start: element 5% to 50% visible depending on section

patterns.exit_behaviour: See rule-retract-exit: origin flips to the right edge and the rule retracts over 700ms.
patterns.interruptible: Guarded by an animatedIn flag, so it only plays once per mount unless explicitly reset.
patterns.applies_to: Hairline dividers on list rows, news rows, link cards, stat blocks, accordion rows and section tops. List rows may use a longer 2000ms draw.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: render rules at full width immediately.
patterns.ux_purpose: Draws the grid before the content lands, like a technical drawing being ruled. It establishes structure and reading direction (left to right) and gives every row a clear start point.

patterns.name: slide-in-from-start

trigger.start: IntersectionObserver threshold 0.05 by default, 0.5 on text-heavy sections

patterns.exit_behaviour: Mirror exit when content is hidden by a parent (for example a tab switch): translateX(+10%) and opacity 0 over 700ms ease-out-expo.
patterns.interruptible: One-shot per mount via an animatedIn flag. If the element is already in the viewport at mount, it animates immediately instead of waiting for the observer.
patterns.applies_to: Content groups inside rows and cards (index label, title, subtitle, media), stat blocks, news rows, link cards, accordion row headers, form fields (variant: 800ms, tight stagger of 50ms per field index).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: opacity-only fade at the fast duration, no translate.
patterns.ux_purpose: The house entrance. A short horizontal push from the reading-start edge, paired with rule-draw, makes lists and cards assemble in reading order and keeps scanning left-aligned and fast. Distance is relative (10% of the element) so small labels move little and large blocks move more.

patterns.name: rule-retract-exit

trigger.start: parent hides the section (tab or filter change)

patterns.exit_behaviour: This is the exit. Content beside it moves +10% on x and fades to 0 in the same 700ms.
patterns.interruptible: Resets the animatedIn flag so the entrance can replay when the section returns.
patterns.applies_to: Accordion rows and list rows inside tabbed containers.
patterns.ux_purpose: Leaving in the reading direction (out to the right) while entering from the left keeps a consistent sense of flow, so swapped content feels like it has been paged forward rather than deleted.

patterns.name: header-scroll-coupled-hide
patterns.exit_behaviour: Scrolling up reveals it at 1:1 with scroll distance. Programmatic hide or show (for immersive sections) tweens over 1000ms ease-in-out-cubic.
patterns.interruptible: Not a toggle: the offset is accumulated from scroll deltas and clamped to 0..1 of header height, so reversing direction mid-hide reverses smoothly. Scroll updates are ignored while a route transition or programmatic tween is running. A reference-counted hider API lets several components request hidden state; it shows again only when all release.
patterns.applies_to: Primary header on every page. Writes a --header-offset CSS variable so sticky sub-navigation follows it.
patterns.responsive_differences: Desktop: downward scroll hides at half rate (header fully hides after 2x its height of scroll), upward reveals at full rate. Mobile (768px and under): 1:1 both ways.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: keep (it is scroll-bound, not autonomous motion).
patterns.ux_purpose: Returns screen space to content as soon as the reader commits to scrolling down, but gives navigation back instantly on any upward intent. Coupling to scroll distance instead of a timed toggle means the header never animates on its own and never fights the reader.

patterns.name: header-frost-on-scroll

trigger.start: scroll > 30px, or any nav item hovered, or mobile menu open

properties.--background-opacity: 0.5 on light variants, 1 on solid-dark variant

patterns.exit_behaviour: Reverses over the same 300ms when back at the top and no menu is open. Resets instantly at the midpoint of a route change.
patterns.interruptible: Values are tweened custom properties, so a new target simply retargets from the current value.
patterns.applies_to: Primary header. Each page declares a header mode (transparent over dark, transparent over light, frosted light, solid dark); text colour switches instantly per mode.
patterns.responsive_differences: Mobile header keeps a minimum 0.3 background opacity on the bar.
patterns.ux_purpose: Keeps the header legible over any content once the page moves, while letting heroes run edge to edge at rest. The per-page mode lets each hero choose the header tone.

patterns.name: mega-menu-height-expand

trigger.start: pointer enters or keyboard focuses a top-level nav item

patterns.exit_behaviour: On leaving the whole nav region (not just the item) height tweens to 0 over 500ms and content fades out 500ms; the company panel fades out slower (1000ms). Panels are display:none after fade.
patterns.interruptible: Moving between sibling items crossfades panels (outgoing 500ms fade, incoming 500ms fade with 100ms delay) while the wrapper height tweens from its current value to the new panel height. A ResizeObserver re-tweens height if the panel content changes.
patterns.applies_to: Desktop primary navigation panels (category menus, company menu, search panel). Search panel focuses its input after its fade completes.
patterns.responsive_differences: Desktop only (769px and up). Mobile uses mobile-menu-slide.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: instant height, keep the opacity crossfade at the fast duration.
patterns.ux_purpose: A single shared panel that morphs in height between sections preserves spatial context: the menu feels like one surface changing content, not several dropdowns opening and closing.

patterns.name: sibling-dim-focus

trigger.start: pointer over or focus on one item in a group

patterns.exit_behaviour: Siblings return to full opacity over 500ms with a 150ms delay when the pointer leaves the group; the hovered item returns to 1 over 150ms.
patterns.interruptible: Retargets from current opacity.
patterns.applies_to: Top-level navigation items; the pattern suits any horizontal set of peer options.
patterns.ux_purpose: Spotlights the active choice by receding the alternatives rather than decorating the target, which keeps the nav typographic and quiet.

patterns.name: nav-scrim-fade
patterns.exit_behaviour: Exits from 0.5 to 0 over 300ms (about 0.5x the entrance) then is hidden.
patterns.interruptible: Retargets.
patterns.applies_to: A full-viewport gradient scrim beneath the desktop header while a nav panel is open.
patterns.ux_purpose: Pushes page content back so the open menu reads as the foreground layer, without a hard modal.

patterns.name: link-underline-draw-replay

trigger.start: 300ms after the link enters view; replays on each pointer over

patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit; underline stays drawn. The whole link sits at a reduced opacity (about 0.6) and rises to full on hover over 300ms.
patterns.interruptible: Replay restarts cleanly: the class is removed, a reflow is forced, and the class is re-added.
patterns.applies_to: Primary text links with trailing arrow icon. First draw is 300ms scaleX 0 to 1 from the left; hover replay is 600ms (wipe out to the right, then redraw from the left). Secondary (outlined) link buttons instead invert fill and text over 300ms.
patterns.responsive_differences: On touch the in-view draw still plays; hover replay never fires.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: underline static at full width.
patterns.ux_purpose: The underline arriving on its own marks links as actionable before any hover. The wipe-through on hover confirms the pointer has registered, with a directional sweep that echoes the rule-draw language.

patterns.name: plus-rotate-toggle
patterns.exit_behaviour: Reverses on collapse over the same 300ms.
patterns.interruptible: CSS transition, retargets naturally.
patterns.applies_to: Expand indicators on nav items with sub-menus, footer link groups (mobile), product feature rows and accordion rows (accordion rows swap a plus icon for a minus icon instead).
patterns.ux_purpose: A plus built from two bars where one bar rotates flat to form a minus. It confirms state change in the exact spot the user clicked, with no layout shift.

patterns.name: close-button-rotate
patterns.exit_behaviour: Rotates back on leave over 300ms.
patterns.interruptible: CSS transition.
patterns.applies_to: Circular close buttons on side panels, profile overlays and modals.
patterns.ux_purpose: A quarter turn on a symmetric cross is a playful but precise confirmation that the control is live; it does not change the icon's meaning.
patterns.snippet:
.close-btn { transition: transform .3s ease-out; }
@media (hover:hover) { .close-btn:hover { transform: rotate(90deg); } }

patterns.name: accordion-fill-wipe

trigger.start: pointer enters a closed accordion row

patterns.exit_behaviour: Wipes back down over 300ms on leave or on open. Row text flips to the contrast tone ({color.on-accent}) instantly while filled; images inside get a filter driven by --filter-progress.
patterns.interruptible: Retargets. Suppressed while the row is open.
patterns.applies_to: Accordion rows and open-role list rows (same wipe via CSS on the list variant).
patterns.ux_purpose: A solid block rising from the baseline makes the whole row feel like one large target and previews that it will open, which is stronger than a colour shift on the text alone.

patterns.name: accordion-height-expand
patterns.exit_behaviour: Collapse tweens height back to the header height over 500ms; preview images fade out over 100ms then become invisible.
patterns.interruptible: Retargets from the current height. Height is recomputed on resize via ResizeObserver.
patterns.applies_to: Accordion rows, location lists, feature lists, tabbed accordions. On open, preview thumbnails fade in 250ms each with a 50ms stagger.
patterns.ux_purpose: Animating the row height (not just revealing content) lets the reader keep their place: rows below slide down smoothly instead of jumping.

patterns.name: card-hover-disclosure

trigger.start: pointer enters card (touch: card enters view)

patterns.exit_behaviour: On leave, the description collapses back to height 0 and icons fade out over 500ms. Collapsing is skipped on mobile, where the description stays open once revealed.
patterns.interruptible: Starts from a fixed set state each time, so rapid hover in and out restarts rather than blends. Also collapses on card resize.
patterns.applies_to: Featured product and destination cards in a mosaic grid. The description text also runs text-scramble-decode over 750ms. Media inside scales slightly (see media-hover-zoom).
patterns.responsive_differences: Touch or 768px and under: reveals once on in-view and stays.
patterns.ux_purpose: Keeps the grid visually clean (titles only) while rewarding intent with a one-line summary. The scramble makes the reveal feel like data surfacing, in keeping with the system.

patterns.name: media-hover-zoom
patterns.exit_behaviour: Returns on leave over the same duration.
patterns.interruptible: CSS transition.
patterns.applies_to: Image inside carousel link cards (1.05), product carousel cards (1.1), resource and profile cards (transform transition 300ms). Mosaic cards use a faster 200ms transform and opacity transition.
patterns.ux_purpose: A slow push-in inside a fixed, clipped frame signals the card is interactive without moving the card itself, so the grid stays rigid.

patterns.name: modal-blur-backdrop
patterns.exit_behaviour: Symmetric: blur 30px to 0 and scrim back to 0 over 1000ms, then display:none.
patterns.interruptible: Tweens retarget from current values.
patterns.applies_to: Centre modals (video player, forms, profiles). Page scroll is paused via a reference-counted Lenis pauser.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: no blur tween; show scrim at target opacity immediately.
patterns.ux_purpose: A slow defocus of the page behind feels like a camera racking focus: the page is still there (spatial context preserved) but clearly out of play.

patterns.name: side-panel-slide
patterns.exit_behaviour: Symmetric 250ms: panel back to 100%, scrim to 0, blur to 0, then hidden. Focus returns to the trigger.
patterns.interruptible: Tweens retarget.
patterns.applies_to: Filter panels, location detail panels, secondary detail drawers.
patterns.responsive_differences: Panel is a fraction of viewport width on desktop and wider on mobile. Horizontal drag of more than 80px to the right closes it.
patterns.ux_purpose: Fast and symmetric because the panel is a quick side trip; the page behind remains in place so the user can return exactly where they were.

patterns.name: mobile-menu-slide
patterns.exit_behaviour: Screens slide back to translateX(100%) over 300ms; focus returns to the menu button.
patterns.interruptible: State-driven and debounced; rapid toggles collapse to the final state.
patterns.applies_to: Mobile navigation. A frosted background layer and the menu screen slide in together from the right; section titles run text-scramble-decode at 600ms and 700ms. Drilling into a sub-menu crossfades screens (opacity 0.5s) and staggers the sub-links in at 300ms + 50ms x index.
patterns.responsive_differences: 768px and under only. Body scroll paused; the menu has its own scroll instance.
patterns.ux_purpose: Moving in from the right edge maps to going deeper; the two-level screen stack (menu, then sub-menu with a back control) keeps each screen short and thumb-friendly.

patterns.name: page-transition-scale-crossfade
patterns.exit_behaviour: Hands over to page-transition-settle-in once the new page is built.
patterns.interruptible: The old page is frozen in place (position fixed at its current scroll offset, transform-origin at the viewport centre) and scroll resets to top instantly before this phase, so there is no visible jump. Header frost resets at the midpoint. A WebGL uniform runs 0 to 1 in step with the overlay.
patterns.applies_to: All internal navigations in the SPA router (pushState). First load skips the transition and shows instantly.
patterns.ux_purpose: A slight push-in on the outgoing page reads as moving forward into the next space, and covers fetch latency.

patterns.name: page-transition-settle-in
patterns.exit_behaviour: Transforms are cleared on complete; the router then flags the transition as finished, which releases hero entrance patterns.
patterns.interruptible: Not interrupted mid-phase; a new navigation starts after the current one resolves.
patterns.applies_to: All internal navigations in the SPA router.
patterns.ux_purpose: The incoming page settles from slightly small to full size, completing one continuous forward motion so the site feels like a single application rather than separate pages.

patterns.name: smooth-scroll-inertia
patterns.exit_behaviour: n/a
patterns.interruptible: Each wheel event retargets the duration-based tween. Programmatic scroll-to (hero down-arrow, anchor links) uses 2500ms with lerp 0.1.
patterns.applies_to: Global document scroll; separate instances for the mobile menu, dropdown lists and search results panels.
patterns.responsive_differences: Wheel only. Touch uses native momentum (syncTouch off).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: disable smoothing (native scroll) when reduced motion is requested.
patterns.ux_purpose: Heavy, damped scrolling gives the long cinematic pages a sense of mass and keeps scroll-linked WebGL in sync; leaving touch native avoids fighting mobile momentum.

patterns.name: carousel-drag-snap

trigger.start: pointer or touch drag on track; arrow keys; prev and next buttons

patterns.exit_behaviour: n/a
patterns.interruptible: Drag cancels any running snap tween and continues from the live position. Past the first or last slide, movement is damped with a friction factor of 0.3 (rubber band). On release: velocity above 1.5 flicks forward by log2(velocity) slides, a smaller velocity steps one slide, otherwise rounds to the nearest slide. Drag is axis-locked so vertical page scroll is not hijacked.
patterns.applies_to: Link carousels, product carousels, quote carousels. Prev and next circle buttons disable (reduced opacity, pointer-events off) at the ends.
patterns.responsive_differences: Desktop drag enabled; touch drag native feel. Arrow keys move one slide.
patterns.ux_purpose: Physical drag with friction and flick momentum makes carousels feel like handling an object, and the snap guarantees every slide rests aligned to the grid.

patterns.name: roller-counter
patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit.
patterns.interruptible: Re-targeting picks the shortest path around a doubled 0 to 9 column (bias factor 1.2 towards the preferred direction), so updates never spin the long way.
patterns.applies_to: Numeric stats and counters, including in-chart values.
patterns.ux_purpose: An odometer roll reads as a measured value arriving, and keeps digit widths fixed so surrounding text does not reflow while counting.

patterns.name: marquee-loop
patterns.exit_behaviour: n/a
patterns.interruptible: Infinite loop; two identical groups placed side by side so the loop seam is invisible. Duration is set per instance via a --duration custom property.
patterns.applies_to: Partner or logo strips.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: pause the marquee (animation-play-state: paused) and allow manual horizontal scroll.
patterns.ux_purpose: Signals breadth (many items) in minimal vertical space, without asking the user to interact.

patterns.name: image-lazy-fade
patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit.
patterns.interruptible: n/a
patterns.applies_to: All responsive images. Aspect ratio is reserved from CMS metadata before load, so there is no layout shift.
patterns.responsive_differences: Different srcset and sizes per breakpoint.
patterns.ux_purpose: Loads just ahead of need and fades in very quickly: enough to avoid a hard pop, too quick to feel like a deliberate animation.

patterns.name: spinner-rotate
patterns.exit_behaviour: Fades out over 300ms when loading ends.
patterns.interruptible: n/a
patterns.applies_to: Inline in buttons that load heavy assets (for example a 3D viewer). A segmented progress icon pulses segments (opacity 1 to 0.2 over 2500ms, linear, infinite) while a 3D asset loads.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: static indicator with a text status.
patterns.ux_purpose: Local, in-place feedback that the specific action is working, without blocking the page.

patterns.name: floating-anchor-button-reveal

trigger.start: a designated section has scrolled above the viewport top

patterns.exit_behaviour: Reverses when scrolled back above the section.
patterns.interruptible: CSS transition; checked every frame.
patterns.applies_to: Fixed bottom-corner square button that returns to a page section (for example back to top of a long article).
patterns.ux_purpose: Appears only once it is useful (the target is out of view), so it never clutters the first screen.

patterns.name: consent-banner-fade

trigger.start: 1000ms after mount, only where consent is legally required

patterns.exit_behaviour: Fades out over 250ms after accept or reject, then removed from layout at 500ms.
patterns.interruptible: n/a
patterns.applies_to: Consent banner (bottom-right, frosted).
patterns.ux_purpose: Delaying the banner lets the first impression land before asking for a decision; the frosted treatment keeps it visually part of the interface.

patterns.name: chart-draw-on-view
patterns.exit_behaviour: No exit.
patterns.interruptible: Guarded by a one-time scrolled flag. Stepped reveals inside charts (titles, details, markers) appear 200ms apart.
patterns.applies_to: SVG data visualisations in long-form editorial pages: lines draw, labels and markers fade in sequence.
patterns.responsive_differences: Mobile variants of complex charts swap to simpler layouts (drag-scrub chart has separate desktop and mobile builds).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Supported: gated by a user-facing animation on/off switch whose default comes from prefers-reduced-motion and is persisted in localStorage. When off, charts render in their final state.
patterns.ux_purpose: Draws data in the order it should be read (lines, then labels, then markers), turning a static chart into a guided explanation.

patterns.name: webgl-dom-sync

properties.uTransition: 0 to 1 to -1 to 0 during route change

patterns.exit_behaviour: Meshes hidden when their section is off screen.
patterns.interruptible: Driven directly by scroll position; no tweens to interrupt.
patterns.applies_to: Hero and feature sections whose media or 3D scenes render in a single fixed full-viewport canvas behind the DOM, positioned to match their DOM placeholders.
patterns.responsive_differences: GPU tier detection selects asset quality; an accessible DOM mirror (visually hidden) carries the text for WebGL-rendered titles.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: render static poster images instead of the live scene.
patterns.ux_purpose: Lets immersive 3D and shader media scroll exactly like normal content, so the page feels continuous rather than a sequence of embedded players.

choreography_rules: Hero order after a route transition: heading lines (100ms stagger), short label decode, and media fade all start together; the heading's steep ease makes it read first.
Within a row or card: the divider rule starts at 0ms, content children follow at a 200ms base delay plus 100ms per child in DOM order (index label, title, subtitle, media last at about +500ms).
Form fields cascade at 50ms per field index, 800ms each.
Sub-menu links cascade at 300ms plus 50ms per index, after the screen swap.
Overlays: the backdrop (blur and scrim) animates first; focus moves to the close control only when the backdrop tween completes.
Menus: the shared panel height and the incoming panel fade run together, with the fade delayed 100ms so content never appears outside the growing container.

Page change: freeze and reset scroll, fade the overlay while the old page scales up, swap, then settle the new page while the overlay fades out. Hero entrances wait for the transition to report finished.
Anything already in the viewport at mount animates immediately; everything else waits for its own in-view trigger. Reveals are one-shot per mount.
Only one hover-driven overlay (a nav panel or the scrim) is ever active; moving between nav items crossfades rather than stacking.

reduced_motion.strategy: An animation on/off switch (role=switch, aria-checked, persisted in localStorage, default derived from prefers-reduced-motion) exists only in the long-form editorial template and only gates data-visualisation animations. The main site's reveals, scrambles, transitions and smooth scroll ignore the preference, and the stylesheet contains no prefers-reduced-motion media queries. Replicas should apply the per-pattern reduced_motion_fallback values globally.

motion_system.performance_notes: Entrances animate transform and opacity (translate percentages, scaleX and scaleY for rules and fills). Height is tweened directly for accordions, mega-menu panels and card descriptions (layout-affecting but short and localised). Backdrop-filter blur is tweened on modals (1000ms), which is GPU-heavy on low-end devices. Header offset and frost are written to CSS custom properties in a per-frame render loop. Text scramble writes textContent at a throttled rate. Images lazy-load 250px ahead with reserved aspect ratios. WebGL runs in one fixed canvas with GPU tier detection selecting asset quality. will-change is used sparingly (row fill backgrounds). Live testing in an automated pane showed the app pausing rendering when not painted, consistent with a requestAnimationFrame-driven loop.

information_architecture.depth: 1 to 2 clicks from the home page to any capability or detail page via the mega menu; long-form editorial and listing pages are reached from featured slots or the company menu.

page_templates.name: landing
page_templates.purpose: Brand statement and routing into capability areas and news.
section_order: full-bleed hero video with masked heading and scroll-down control

page_templates.name: capability detail

page_templates.name: long-form editorial

navigation.primary: Fixed top bar. Transparent over heroes at rest (tone set per page), frosts after 30px of scroll or on any nav hover. Hides in proportion to scroll (desktop hides at half the scroll rate, reveals at full rate on scroll up). Hovering or focusing a top-level item dims siblings, fades in a page scrim and expands one shared mega panel whose height morphs between sections. Search lives in the same panel system and receives focus when opened. When hidden programmatically the header is made inert.
navigation.mobile: Compact bar (72px tall) with menu and search buttons. Menu slides in from the right as a frosted full-screen layer with its own scroll; sections drill into a second screen with a back control and staggered links. Page scroll is paused. Custom Tab focus trap keeps focus inside the open menu; closing returns focus to the menu button.
navigation.secondary: Optional sticky in-page secondary navigation below the header (follows the header via a --header-offset custom property); in-page anchor deep links (the section more than 50% in view is tracked as the current deep link); footer with link groups that collapse into plus-toggled accordions on mobile; floating anchor button on long pages.
navigation.wayfinding: Current section tracked by in-view share; route changes announced by the top progress bar; per-page header tone signals context. No breadcrumbs or scroll progress bar observed.

steps: Open form (inline slice or modal triggered by an action button)
Fill fields; phone input filters characters live
Client-side validation runs across all fields at once
On failure: inline field errors plus a form-level message
On success: form hidden, confirmation shown, fields cleared
entry_points: Action buttons configured to open a form
user_flows.exit_and_recovery: Server error shows a generic retry message in place; entered values are kept. No loading state on the submit button.

steps: Hover or focus a top-level nav item
friction_reducers: Instant scroll reset hidden behind the transition
user_flows.exit_and_recovery: Browser back uses the same router and transition.

steps: Open search in the nav panel (desktop) or search mode in the mobile menu
Results panel resizes to fit results
Select a result (closes menu and navigates)
friction_reducers: Results in place without leaving the page
user_flows.exit_and_recovery: Leaving the nav region or toggling search closes it.

forms.error_presentation: Message text directly below each invalid field, field container marked invalid, plus a form-level message near the submit control. Specific messages for email, month, phone and profile URL formats; otherwise a configurable required message.
forms.success_presentation: Form container hidden and a confirmation block shown in place; all fields cleared.
forms.required_indicator: Native required attribute set; visual indicator not confirmed (see gaps).
forms.input_assistance: Live character filtering on phone input, max lengths per type, auto-growing textarea, searchable single and multi-select dropdowns with their own scroll, file upload with type limits, country list select.

feedback_and_states.perceived_performance: Thin top progress bar with decelerating fake progress; route changes hidden behind a 700ms scale-crossfade; images lazy-load 250px early with reserved aspect ratios and a 125ms fade; heavy 3D assets show a segmented pulsing loader and an in-button spinner.
feedback_and_states.empty_states: Not observed (listing filters with no results not tested).
feedback_and_states.errors: Inline form errors in an error tone; form-level generic error on network failure. Unsupported browsers are redirected to a static fallback page before the app loads.
feedback_and_states.toasts_and_notifications: None. A consent banner (bottom-right) and a content preview banner are the only notification-like surfaces.
feedback_and_states.confirmations: None needed (no destructive actions on a marketing site).

attention_and_hierarchy.cta_strategy: Primary actions are understated text links with an arrow and a self-drawing underline; secondary actions are outlined boxes. CTAs repeat per section rather than sticking to the viewport. A single floating square anchor button may appear on long pages.
attention_and_hierarchy.attention_direction: The masked heading reveal wins the first beat of each page; rules then draw left to right and content slides in from the left in DOM order, walking the eye down and across each row. Scrambled labels create brief points of flicker that pull attention to category and metadata text.
attention_and_hierarchy.progressive_disclosure: Mega menu panels, card descriptions, accordion content, mobile sub-menus, filter drawers and fullscreen 3D viewers are all hidden until intent (hover, focus or tap).

breakpoint_behaviour.changes: Mobile header and menu replace desktop nav; header hides 1:1 with scroll; accordion hover fill disabled; card descriptions reveal on in-view instead of hover; footer link groups collapse into accordions; charts switch to mobile builds; filters move into drawers.
Desktop nav and hover behaviours; some grids tighten.
Larger scale for type and spacing; motion unchanged.
Specific adjustments for landscape phones (inferred from media queries).

responsive_behaviour.touch_adaptations: Hover effects gated by (hover: hover); circle buttons use touchstart and touchend to show a pressed state; native touch scrolling (smooth scroll disabled for touch); swipe-to-close on side panels; drag with axis lock on carousels; pinch and gesture events blocked in the fullscreen 3D viewer.

accessibility.focus_visibility: Mostly relies on browser default focus rings; only four custom focus-visible rules exist. Several controls remove outlines entirely (mobile menu button, some filter and text inputs replace the outline with a border change).
accessibility.semantics: Landmarks nav, header, main and footer present. Heading order starts with h3 elements in the navigation before the page h1. Navigation category triggers and accordion rows are div elements with click handlers rather than buttons.
accessibility.screen_reader_notes: WebGL-rendered titles have a visually hidden DOM mirror. Decorative icons are aria-hidden. Split text keeps an aria-label on the original element by default. Scrambled text writes random characters into live text nodes during animation, which screen readers may announce if they read mid-animation.
issues_found: No Escape key handling for any menu, panel or modal.
Generic modal lacks role dialog, aria-modal and a focus trap.
Top-level nav triggers are div role=link without aria-expanded or aria-controls.
Accordion rows are clickable divs with a non-standard role value; not operable by keyboard.
Positive tabindex on the animation switch and on the desktop mega menu (tabindex values renumbered dynamically).
Mobile menu button removes focus-visible outline.
Reduced motion preference ignored outside long-form data visualisations; no prefers-reduced-motion CSS.
Form errors are not programmatically linked to inputs (no aria-invalid or aria-describedby) and focus is not moved to the first error.
Circle buttons are about 34px square (8px padding around a 16px icon plus border), under the 44px guideline (inferred from CSS).

do: Use ease-out-expo at 1000 to 1500ms for entrances and 700ms for reveal exits.
Pair every list row or card with a rule-draw from the left edge.
Offset content entrances by translateX(-10%) of the element, never a fixed pixel distance.
Stagger siblings at 100ms after a 200ms base delay; use 50ms for dense lists such as form fields and sub-menu links.
Use text-scramble-decode for short uppercase labels and one-line descriptions only, and always restore the clean string at the end.
Mask heading lines and translate them from 100% on y, 100ms apart.
Tie the header's hidden offset to accumulated scroll delta and clamp it; reveal at full rate on upward scroll.
Morph one shared menu panel in height between sections instead of opening separate dropdowns.
Animate overlay backdrops first and move focus only after the backdrop completes.
Freeze the outgoing page and reset scroll before a route transition so the swap never jumps.
Trigger in-view reveals immediately for elements already on screen at mount.
Gate hover-only reveals with (hover: hover) and provide an in-view equivalent on touch.
Add Escape to close, real buttons with aria-expanded, and prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks (the source lacks these; the replica should not).
dont: Do not use springs, overshoot or bounce easing; the feel is damped and heavy.
Do not lift, tilt or add glow to cards on hover; only media inside a clipped frame may scale.
Do not fade content up from below as the default entrance; the house direction is horizontal from the reading-start edge.
Do not scramble body copy or headings longer than a line; it becomes unreadable noise.
Do not animate the header on a timer or toggle it at a fixed threshold.
Do not replay scroll reveals every time an element re-enters the viewport.
Do not use short (under 300ms) durations for entrances; they break the cinematic pacing.
Do not stack multiple overlays or scrims; crossfade between them.
Do not hijack touch scrolling with smoothing.
Do not ship hover-only affordances without a touch alternative.

implementation.target_stack: Next.js (App Router, client components) + Tailwind CSS + GSAP 3 (with SplitText) + Lenis 1.3. Assumed because the target stack field was left unfilled; every snippet is a plain ES module usable inside a 'use client' component or useEffect.
recommended_libraries: gsap (core + SplitText) as the tween engine; its expo, power and sine eases map 1:1 to the source curves
lenis 1.3.x for duration-based wheel smoothing with native touch
three.js only if replicating the WebGL-synced media layer (optional)

ai_replication_prompt: You are implementing a cinematic, restrained motion system called Mission-Console Cinematic Motion. Import motion-tokens.js and motion-presets.js and use only their tokens. Entrances use ease-out-expo: content groups slide in with slide-in-from-start (translateX(-10%) plus opacity, 1000ms, 200ms base delay, 100ms stagger in DOM order) while their divider runs rule-draw (scaleX from the left edge, 1500ms). Trigger reveals once per mount with a 5% IntersectionObserver threshold (50% for text-heavy sections), and animate immediately if the element is already on screen. The single primary heading per page uses hero-line-mask-reveal (masked lines from y 100%, 1000ms, 100ms apart) after the page transition finishes; hero media uses hero-media-fade. Short uppercase labels and one-line descriptions use text-scramble-decode (500ms, ease-in-out-sine progress, random letters for text or digits for numbers, spaces and punctuation preserved, clean text restored). Numbers use roller-counter. Reveal exits run at about half the entrance duration and move the other way (rule-retract-exit, +10%, origin on the right edge, 700ms). Hover feedback is typographic: link-underline-draw-replay on text links, sibling-dim-focus in nav groups, accordion-fill-wipe on rows, media-hover-zoom inside clipped frames, close-button-rotate on close icons, plus-rotate-toggle for expand icons. Never lift cards, never use springs or bounce. Navigation: header-scroll-coupled-hide (offset from accumulated scroll delta, half rate down on desktop, full rate up), header-frost-on-scroll after 30px, one shared mega-menu-height-expand panel with nav-scrim-fade, and mobile-menu-slide on small screens. Overlays: modal-blur-backdrop (1000ms, symmetric) and side-panel-slide (250ms ease-in-out-quad, symmetric); animate the backdrop first, then focus the close control; Escape closes; focus returns to the trigger. Route changes use page-transition-scale-crossfade (freeze old page, reset scroll, scale 1 to 1.02 and overlay in over 350ms ease-out-sine) then page-transition-settle-in (scale 0.98 to 1 and overlay out over 350ms ease-in-sine) with page-load-progress-bar. Scrolling uses smooth-scroll-inertia on wheel only. Carousels use carousel-drag-snap. Gate every hover reveal with (hover: hover) and give touch an in-view equivalent. Respect prefers-reduced-motion using each pattern's reduced_motion_fallback. Use real buttons with aria-expanded for every disclosure.

gaps.issue: None supplied. Timing comes from code; perceived choreography across a full scroll was not recorded.
gaps.suggested_approach: Capture a 60fps recording of a slow then fast scroll on the landing page and one route change to confirm the relative start times of overlapping patterns.

gaps.issue: The automated browser pane paused requestAnimationFrame when not painting, so screenshots timed out and runtime header offsets were stale. Visual behaviour was reconstructed from the application bundle and stylesheet instead.
gaps.suggested_approach: Re-run the interaction sweep in a foreground desktop browser and log the header --header-offset variable and document.getAnimations() during scroll.

gaps.suggested_approach: Record the scramble at high frame rate and count distinct character changes per second.

gaps.issue: The target stack field in the brief was left as a placeholder, so Next.js + Tailwind + GSAP + Lenis was assumed.
gaps.suggested_approach: Tell me the actual stack and the snippets can be re-expressed (for example Framer Motion variants or plain CSS).
